subject: Post-demo recap + evaluation sprint scope for NimbusAI
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Lea Park <lea@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-11T14:10:00Z
Subject: Post-demo recap + initial evaluation scope

Lea — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side to make sure we’re aligned and to capture the next steps we discussed.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Latency spikes on long-context retrieval flows (500–2,000 tokens) during peak hours (~3–5x baseline).
- Cost pressure on per-token spend for high-throughput embedding pipelines (clinical triage workload).
- Need for deterministic behavior around model-version pinning for compliance audits.

Goals you want to hit in the POC:
1) 95th pct latency < 250ms at median production sequence length (650 tokens) for read-only inference.
2) 40–60% token-cost reduction vs current unmanaged endpoints via caching + batching and quantization paths.
3) Audit-ready logs and model pinning; ability to produce audit artifact for any inference in <72 hours.

Open questions we promised to follow up on:
- Can you share a small representative sample of the long-context requests (anonymized) so we can simulate your latency profile? (Lea — you mentioned Jordan on procurement could help with sanitized data.)
- Confirmation of max acceptable cold-start window for Canary rollouts (you said ~90s).
- Which embedding dimension and batching cadence does the triage pipeline use?

Proposed evaluation sprint (high-level):
- Week 0: data handoff + baseline measurements on your sample set (we run identical payloads against Nimbus and Redwood in our env).
- Week 1: targeted optimizations (KV prefix caching, sequence-length-aware batching) + cost projection.
- Week 2: compliance artifact run — model pinning + audit logs + SLA smoke tests.

Deliverables: test harness results, per-token cost delta, decision matrix (us vs. Nimbus vs. VertexCloud), and an internal runbook for the POC.

Attachments: nimbus-eval-questions.docx (simple questionnaire), redwood-poc-plan.pdf (POC timeline + success criteria).

Next steps: Lea to share sanitized sample and confirm procurement contact for NDAs/data transfer (Jordan?). We’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff the week of 5/17.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-poc-plan.pdf]
[Attachment: nimbus-eval-questions.docx]

From: Lea Park <lea@nimbus.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + initial evaluation scope

Alex — appreciate the clear recap. Confirming a few items from our side:

- We can provide an anonymized subset of production traces (approx. 1,200 requests) by EOD 5/13. Jordan will own the handoff and the sanitized export.
- Embedding dims: 1,024; triage batching cadence: ~250ms peak batching window; current 95th pct latency target for us is 300ms (we’d like to get to 250ms if possible).
- Cold-start tolerance: we can accept up to 120s during rollouts but would prefer sub-90s.

We reviewed your proposed sprint and it looks good. A few asks from our procurement/security teams:
1) Temporary SOC-equivalent checklist and an NDA template (Jordan attached the procurement contact).
2) A simple cost model with assumptions about tokenization and expected concurrency for the triage workload.

I’ll confirm the data export and NDA timeline with Jordan. Kickoff the week of 5/17 is fine — Tue or Wed morning (ET) preferred.

-Lea
Lea Park
Head of Platform Integrations
NimbusAI
[Attachment: nimbus-procurement-contacts.pdf]

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-12T13:30:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap + initial evaluation scope (Nimbus) — recommended eval plan + competitive checklist

Folks — forwarding the thread with Lea. Summary / internal readout and asks:

Summary:
- Nimbus asked for a 2–3 week POC focused on latency, cost delta, and compliance artifacts. They can deliver sanitized traces by 5/13 via Jordan.
- Key metrics: 95th pct latency target ~250–300ms; embeddings dim 1,024; batching cadence ~250ms.

Competitive notes (quick):
- VertexCloud historically wins on cold-start but has worse per-token economics on embedding-heavy workloads unless aggressively quantized.
- Nimbus claims their caching layer helps long-context, but we should run a head-to-head on prefix/KV cache hit patterns — that’s likely the differentiation.

Proposed internal plan (short):
1) Build the harness to replay their 1,200 traces against: a) Nimbus demo instance (if they provide), b) Redwood in our evaluation mesh, c) VertexCloud (our sandbox).
2) Baseline run: identical concurrency + tokenization. Capture per-request latency, KV-cache hit ratio, and token-cost estimate.
3) Optimization run: enable Redwood prefix caching + sequence-length-aware batching + 8-bit quant path (if accuracy delta acceptable).

I’ve attached a quick heatmap template (nimbus-vs-vertex-heatmap.xlsx). Please review and add any extra tests you want included. Need volunteers to run the baseline harness and to own analysis.

Requests:
- Marissa: can you lead the POC analysis and own the decision matrix?
- Sergio: can you own the harness runs and automation (k6 + replay scripts)?

Timeline: baseline by 5/21, optimization runs complete by 5/28, internal readout 5/31.

Thanks — Alex

[Attachment: nimbus-vs-vertex-heatmap.xlsx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-13T08:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo recap + initial evaluation scope (Nimbus) — recommended eval plan + competitive checklist

All — I reviewed Alex’s plan and added a few rows to the heatmap. Quick notes and assignments below.

Decision matrix axes (proposed):
- Latency (P50/P95/P99), Cost delta (normalized $/1M tokens), Stability (error rate over 24h), Operational overhead (engineering hours, deployment complexity), Compliance readiness (time to artifact).

Test additions:
- Long-tail cold-start test: 10x warm-to-cold transitions over a 2-hour window (measures cold-start distribution).
- Cache eviction char test: run a sustained 12-hour trace at 2x nominal throughput to observe cache churn and eviction impacts.
- Accuracy check: sample 200 calls to verify quantized vs FP32 correctness (watch for hallucination drift in triage labels).

Assignments:
- Marissa (me): own decision matrix + stakeholder readout deck (deliverable by 5/31).
- Sergio: harness automation + baseline runs (target baseline complete 5/21).
- Alex: coordinate data handoff with Lea/Jordan and maintain the POC timeline.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Nimbus may not provide a production-like cache configuration. Mitigation: we’ll run both their suggested config and a Redwood-optimized config to keep apples-to-apples.
- Risk: sanitized traces may lose meaningful context. Mitigation: ask Jordan for a mapping table and retention policy summary.

I’ll push an initial decision-matrix draft to the drive link and update the heatmap. Alex — once Jordan confirms the export, schedule the kickoff and add the HubSpot deal to the calendar invite.

-Marissa
Director, Solutions Strategy
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: updated-nimbus-heatmap.xlsx]
